summary: Month-end forecasted overage vs final invoice: credit adjustment missing after dedicated burst events
description:
Issue summary:
Customer TextFlow.ai saw a large difference between the usage forecast in the Console (estimated overage ~1.8M tokens) shown during month-end and the actual invoice line which recorded ~600k tokens with a later unexplained credit reversal. Customer claims credits we agreed on during a preliminary billing review were not reflected on the final invoice.

Impact:
- TextFlow reports a $2.4k shortfall between expected credits and invoice adjustments.
- They are disputing the invoice and pausing plan renewal conversations until clarified.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (org: textflow-prod, subaccount: analytics)
- Region: us-east-1
- Affected timeframe: 2026-02-28 22:00 UTC through 2026-03-01 03:00 UTC (month-end burst window)

Observed:
- Console forecasted a peak that would push usage into overage and included an automatic suggested credit (preliminary) for 1.2M tokens of burst that should have been covered by reserved-commit credits.
- Final invoice shows base usage ~600k tokens and a later manual credit of only $150 applied; no automated credit matching the forecasted burst.

Expected:
- Forecast that included reserved-capacity credits should match final invoice adjustments, or at minimum a reconciliation note explaining differences.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In org textflow-prod, enable month-end usage forecast in Console > Billing for the month of Feb 2026.
2) Trigger a dedicated-burst job that scales pool from 6->12 GPUs for 20 minutes using the analytics subaccount keys (this mirrors customer's observed job).
3) Wait for billing-export job to run (hourly) and check billing-exporter/exports for the token-tagging lines.
4) Compare Console forecasted overage and "final" exported invoice CSV and reserved-credits reconciliation file.

investigation_notes:
- 2026-03-10 14:20: Support matched customer's export rows against billing-exporter output. Noted that burst allocations during 22:12-22:35 UTC were tagged with org-level tag (textflow-prod) rather than subaccount (analytics). That mismatch prevents automated application of reserved-subaccount credits in the reconciliation job.
- 2026-03-10 17:05: Engineering (SRE) reproduced tag mismatch in staging by forcing autoscaler to route tasks through burst-capacity host pools; billing-exporter was reading instance metadata that sometimes contained only org tag when ephemeral burst nodes attached.
- Probable root cause: race between autoscaler attach and instance tag propagation; billing-exporter reads metadata slightly before the subaccount tag is applied.
- Related PR to add retry/read-after-delay in exporter created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-exporter/pull/482
- Confirmed that when exporter reprocessed the missing window after patch, tokens were re-classified to the analytics subaccount and the reserved-credit logic applied correctly.

Added telemetry to detect future misses and alert if >0.1% of tokens in a window are tagged at org-level while originating from a subaccount namespace.
resolution:
Root cause: billing-exporter read instance metadata before subaccount tag propagation during dedicated burst autoscaler events; tokens were attributed to org-level and missed reserved-subaccount crediting.
Fix: Deployed billing-exporter v1.8.3 with read-after-delay retry and reprocessed affected export window. Billing applied credit memo CM-2026-1182 for $2,360 and adjusted invoice INV-2026-3317.
Follow-up: Create INT task to add end-to-end test covering autoscaler tag propagation and add grafana alert for tag-mismatch rate (INT-9382). Customer notified and confirmed resolution.
